drafter.private_reasoning: The client's settlement floor is confidential and should not appear in the draft or cover note. The purchase price has not been agreed, so the draft should leave it open rather than imply agreement.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Bellweather team — attached is a first-pass revision clarifying the price, closing, representations, and indemnity provisions. The purchase price remains open for discussion. Please send your proposed price and any disclosure schedules so we can move the draft forward promptly.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller the purchase price for the Shares in an amount to be agreed by the parties in writing before this Agreement is executed (the “Purchase Price”). Payment shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after this Agreement is signed, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the closing conditions agreed by the parties in this Agreement. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to complete Closing promptly.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer are accurate in all material respects, subject to the disclosures expressly identified in the schedules to this Agreement.

4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from a breach of the Seller’s representations in this Agreement or liabilities of the Seller existing before Closing that were not disclosed in the schedules to this Agreement. The parties shall agree on the applicable claim procedures, survival period, and liability limitations before execution.

drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We understand Meridian needs the financial statements, supporting diligence materials, and proposed disclosure schedules before proposing a price. We will coordinate their delivery through a secure diligence process and identify any outstanding items. We have also marked the draft with proposed closing conditions and indemnity mechanics for discussion. The purchase price remains open; neither party would be bound until a definitive agreement is executed.

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after this Agreement is signed, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing, subject to: (a) the material accuracy of each party’s representations at Closing; (b) each party’s material performance of its pre-Closing obligations; (c) receipt of any required governmental approvals and absence of any order prohibiting Closing; and (d) delivery of the closing documents specified in this Agreement. A party may waive a condition for its benefit in writing. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to complete Closing promptly.
edits.name: Proposed closing conditions

edits.text: Seller to provide financial statements, supporting diligence materials, and proposed disclosure schedules through the agreed secure diligence process. The parties should settle the scope and cutoff date of the schedules before execution.
edits.name: Diligence and disclosure schedules

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Subject to the limitations below, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from a breach of the Seller’s representations in this Agreement or liabilities of the Seller existing before Closing that were not disclosed in the schedules to this Agreement. A claimant shall give reasonably prompt written notice describing the claim and estimated loss, if known; delay shall reduce recovery only to the extent the indemnifying party is materially prejudiced. The indemnifying party may assume the defense of a third-party claim with reasonably acceptable counsel, provided it acknowledges its indemnity obligation; it may not settle a claim imposing a nonmonetary obligation or admission on the indemnified party without that party’s consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. For discussion, claims for breaches of general representations must be noticed within twelve months after Closing, and aggregate liability for such claims is capped at ten percent of the Purchase Price, subject to a deductible of one percent of the Purchase Price. These time and monetary limits do not apply to fraud. The parties will identify any fundamental representations and applicable exceptions before execution.
edits.name: Proposed indemnity procedures and limits
